skill.name: url-analysis
skill.description: Validate URLs and review link context for content, documentation, SEO, and security checks.
skill.summary: Checks URL accessibility, redirects, and contextual link quality.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in SKILL.md are Markdown documentation false positives, including code fences and sample URLs. The confirmed risk is the Python helper script making unrestricted outbound requests to user-supplied or extracted URLs, which can enable internal endpoint probing if run on untrusted input.

remediation.suggestion: Block localhost, private, link-local, and metadata-service address ranges before making requests. Consider an allowlist or explicit confirmation for external targets.
Update SKILL.md to reference scripts/validate-urls.py, or rename the bundled file to match the documented scripts/validate_urls.py command.

remediation.issue: Network behavior is not clearly gated
remediation.suggestion: State that validation sends outbound requests and should not be run on untrusted documents without review. Keep timeout and redirect limits explicit.

content.value_statement: Broken links and mismatched destinations reduce trust in published content. This skill checks URL health, redirects, and link context so teams can fix issues before release.
actual_capabilities: Extracts HTTP and HTTPS URLs from provided text files using a Python helper script.
Validates one URL or all URLs found in a file.
Checks HTTP status codes, accessibility, redirects, and redirect chain length.
Returns structured validation results for each detected URL.
Guides contextual review of link text, relevance, source authority, and HTTPS usage.
limitations: The helper script uses HEAD requests, which some sites reject or handle differently.
The script does not block localhost, private, or metadata-service addresses.
Contextual relevance depends on available page information and model judgment.
SKILL.md documents scripts/validate_urls.py, but the bundled file is scripts/validate-urls.py.

use_cases.title: Audit Documentation Links
use_cases.description: Check Markdown or help content for broken links, redirects, and destinations that no longer match surrounding text.

use_cases.title: Review SEO Link Quality
use_cases.description: Find redirect chains, outdated targets, and weak link text before publishing or refreshing search content.

use_cases.title: Screen External References
use_cases.description: Review external links for HTTPS usage, suspicious destinations, and context mismatches before release.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Links
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation for a short document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the URLs in this document. Report broken links, redirects, and simple fixes for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Review Link Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these links and their surrounding text. Identify links where the destination does not match the user expectation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Documentation Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Publication review for docs or support content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this documentation page for link quality. Include status, redirects, HTTPS usage, link text quality, and recommended updates.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Link Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this link inventory. Group issues by severity, explain user impact, and recommend a cleanup order for the team.

output_examples.input: Validate links in a blog post before publication.
output_examples.output: A link audit that lists working links, broken links, redirects, slow responses, and suggested replacements.

output_examples.input: Check whether product documentation links match their anchor text.
output_examples.output: A contextual review that flags vague anchors, outdated destinations, homepage links, and more specific alternatives.

output_examples.input: Review external references in a release note.
output_examples.output: A prioritized issue list covering HTTPS status, suspicious domains, redirect chains, and links that need editorial review.

best_practices: Review extracted URLs before running live validation on untrusted documents.
Update redirected links to their final destination when the target is stable.
Check both technical status and whether the linked page matches the surrounding text.
anti_patterns: Do not run the helper script against untrusted files without reviewing extracted URLs.
Do not treat a successful HTTP response as proof that a link is contextually correct.
Do not ignore redirects, because long chains can slow users and hide stale links.

faq.question: Does this skill make network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script uses outbound HTTP requests to validate URLs when the user runs it.

faq.question: Can it validate links in Markdown files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can extract HTTP and HTTPS URLs from a text file, including Markdown content.

faq.question: Does it check redirects?
faq.answer: Yes. The script follows redirects and reports the final URL and redirect chain length.

faq.question: Can it judge whether a link is relevant?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for contextual review, but final relevance depends on available page content and user judgment.

faq.question: Is it safe to run on untrusted documents?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review extracted URLs first because the script can request internal or sensitive network targets.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
